summary: Complete the frozen upload-security architecture with bounded MIME/archive/parser validation, full-content fail-closed malware scanning, immutable tenant-scoped security evidence, revocable re-scan semantics and authorized release capabilities consumed by Task 031.

impacts.evidence: Upload state and security evidence remain organization/workspace scoped under forced RLS. Object keys derive from authenticated scope and UploadID; current release references bind tenant-owned record version and evidence and cannot be manufactured by clients.

Immutable evidence contains only bounded machine outcomes, MIME/extension, sizes/hashes and scanner version identifiers. Raw file contents, archive names, parser excerpts, scanner logs and credential-shaped metadata are excluded from evidence/events.
Task 088b adds no public HTTP operation or generated SDK method. Import/export continues through the internal ReleasedObjectRef capability boundary.
Versioned additive security.upload.decision.v1, security.upload.released.v1 and security.upload.rescan_requested.v1 contracts are registered; existing quarantine event remains unchanged.
Malware scanner and storage ports are host platform capabilities and do not enter Connector SDK v1 or provider-specific contracts.
Expand migration 000023 adds append-only upload_security_evidence, forced RLS, same-tenant evidence linkage and replaces the 088a temporary trigger with the complete security state-transition guard.

Release requires current CLEAN evidence after path/MIME/archive/parser checks and a scanner that consumes the entire immutable object. Scanner errors fail closed; re-scan revokes existing release before new scan work; stale ReleasedObjectRef values fail current-state validation.

Security release is an automated content-safety capability, not a business or legally significant write approval. No manual bypass/override path is introduced; future administrative exceptions would require separate Task-017 risk policy.
Every scan decision is immutable evidence linked to the upload and every decision/release/rescan mutation enqueues bounded versioned outbox evidence in the same PostgreSQL transaction.

Pipeline processing is resumable by canonical state. Scanner outage keeps SCANNING for retry by default; terminal evidence attempts are unique per tenant/upload/attempt; re-scan creates a new evidence/version before release can be recreated.
Upload scanning performs no arbitrary webhook egress. The concrete ClamAV adapter connects only to operator-owned configuration and never accepts an upload/client supplied network endpoint.

The pipeline exposes bounded process and malware_scan observations with outcome, bytes and duration while keeping scanner logs/content out of metric labels. Production scanner/storage latency SLOs remain deployment qualification.

Migration is expand/high-risk with backup checkpoint. Rollback disables new release/scans rather than deleting evidence. A promotion whose DB release commit fails remains an unreachable private-store orphan because canonical state does not become RELEASED.

Adversarial tests cover traversal, MIME mismatch, archive ratio/depth, parser depth/DTD, synthetic malware, scanner outage/retry, partial scanner reads, stale release revocation and ClamAV INSTREAM framing without using real malware.
